author: Dr. Jagadeesh G
text:
We are #hiring for a higher level position at Smart Bhujal.

Recently graduated PhDs preferred but Masters' students with strong profiles will also also considered.

Apply here: https://lnkd.in/dH5bKiAZ

Geospatial Engineer (Remote Sensing + Software)

We are hiring a Geospatial Engineer to build remote sensing and machine learning systems for water - turning satellite imagery into decision support our customers actually use. You should be comfortable with Earth observation data at scale, deep learning, and shipping real software.

Responsibilities:
- Build ML pipelines on satellite imagery (Sentinel-1/2, Landsat, MODIS) including cloud masking, harmonization across sensors, and gap-filled analysis-ready time series
- Train deep learning models on Earth observation data: semantic segmentation for surface water and crop extent, change detection, and time-series classification over long optical/SAR stacks
- Work with InSAR for land deformation, processing interferograms and turning subsidence signals into usable indicators
- Derive evapotranspiration and soil moisture products from imagery (SEBAL/SSEBop-family approaches, SMAP downscaling) and validate them against ground data
- Fuse coarse and fine sensors (GRACE/GRACE-FO storage anomalies, thermal, passive microwave) into consistent products through spatial and temporal downscaling
- Evaluate and fine-tune geospatial foundation models (Prithvi, Clay and similar) against task-specific baselines, and know when the smaller model wins
- Operate at scale on cloud-native geospatial stacks: Google Earth Engine, STAC catalogs, COGs, xarray/rioxarray/Dask, Zarr
- Build the customer-facing layer: decision support tools and dashboards that turn imagery and model outputs into something a client can act on, including map views, time-series explorers, alerting, scenario comparison and report exports
- Ship models as services into the platform with inference APIs, retraining schedules and versioned artifacts, so a model that works in a notebook keeps working in production
